speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To begin, could you please describe your symptoms and medical history in your own words? I need to understand how long these issues have been present and if anything makes them better or worse.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. To help me narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have a history of alcohol use, and have you experienced any other symptoms like numbness, tingling, or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Natalizumab use in Crohn's disease raises a significant concern for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). To evaluate this possibility, I need to check your immune status.

REQUEST TEST: JC_Virus_Index

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal JC virus index makes PML unlikely, so I need to explore other causes for your right-sided ataxia and clumsiness. Have you experienced any recent headaches, vision changes, or difficulty with balance that seems to be worsening over days or weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, along with right-sided weakness and ataxia, I need to visualize the brain to rule out demyelinating lesions or other structural causes.

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_With_Contrast

DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
